Name: [ Reveal controls ] Verify first tap reveals the controls overlay without toggling playback
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Observe the player before tapping
2. Tap the center of the screen once
Expected Results:
- Before the first tap, no controls overlay is shown
- The first tap reveals the controls overlay
- Playback is unaffected — the video keeps playing
- The first tap is not a no-op and does not pause

Name: [ Dismiss overlay ] Verify tapping outside the button dismisses the overlay without pausing
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Reveal the controls overlay
2. Tap outside the center button (empty area)
Expected Results:
- The controls overlay dismisses
- The video keeps playing
- Tapping outside never pauses the video

Name: [ Auto-dismiss ] Verify the overlay auto-dismisses about 1 second after the last interaction
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Reveal the controls overlay
2. Do not touch anything and wait
Expected Results:
- The overlay auto-dismisses after about 1 second
- The overlay does not linger for 3 seconds

Name: [ Pause ] Verify the center button pauses a recorded video and shows the seek controls
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Reveal the controls overlay
2. Tap the center [ play/pause button ]
Expected Results:
- The video pauses
- A [ play icon ] is shown
- The [ ±10s seek buttons ] are present (recorded content)
- The paused overlay persists
AC Covered: UC1a AC-02, UC1a AC-04, UC1b AC-04

Name: [ Paused state ] Verify the paused overlay persists and tapping outside does not resume
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Pause the video
2. Wait about 2 seconds without touching
3. Tap outside the button
Expected Results:
- The paused overlay does not auto-dismiss on the 1s idle timer
- Tapping outside while paused does not resume playback
- The video stays paused

Name: [ Resume ] Verify resuming continues from the exact paused position
Description: Recorded-LS resume position is an open assumption — observe, do not fail the case on it
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Note the timecode where the video is paused
2. Tap the [ play button ] to resume
Expected Results:
- Playback resumes from the same position
- The video does not restart from the beginning

Name: [ Auto-dismiss ] Verify a control interaction resets the 1 second auto-dismiss countdown
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Reveal the overlay
2. Wait about half a second, then tap a control once
Expected Results:
- The interaction restarts the ~1s countdown
- The overlay stays visible because there was interaction

Name: [ Race ] Verify a pause tap wins against the auto-dismiss timer
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Reveal the overlay
2. Tap pause exactly as the overlay is about to dismiss
Expected Results:
- The pause registers
- The expiring timer does not swallow the pause

Name: [ Buffering ] Verify tapping during buffering shows the real loading state
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The network can be throttled to force buffering
Steps:
1. Throttle the network or seek to an unloaded point to force buffering
2. Tap the screen during buffering
Expected Results:
- A real loading / buffering state is shown
- The center button does not show a false [ play icon ]

Name: [ Backgrounding ] Verify backgrounding pauses playback and does not auto-resume
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. While playing, send the app to the background
2. Return to the foreground
3. Repeat while the video is paused
Expected Results:
- Backgrounding while playing pauses via the OS and dismisses the overlay
- Returning to the foreground does not auto-resume
- Backgrounding while paused keeps it paused

Name: [ Surface parity ] Verify reveal, dismiss, pause and resume behave the same on every surface
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps: 1. Repeat reveal / dismiss / pause / resume on each surface (feed player, fullscreen)
Expected Results:
- Behaviour is identical on every surface
- No surface diverges

Name: [ Skip ] Verify the ±10s buttons skip about 10 seconds while playing
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Play to 1:00
2. Tap the [ −10s button ]
3. Return to 1:00 and tap the [ +10s button ]
Expected Results:
- −10s jumps to about 0:50
- +10s jumps to about 1:10
- Each skip moves about 10 seconds

Name: [ Skip boundary ] Verify skip-back near the start clamps to 0:00
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Go to about 0:05 and tap [ −10s ]
2. Go to 0:00 and tap [ −10s ]
3. Repeat while paused
Expected Results:
- Skip-back near the start clamps to 0:00
- At 0:00 it stays at 0:00
- The clamp behaves the same while paused

Name: [ Skip boundary ] Verify skip-forward at the end stops on the final frame without looping
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Play near the end
2. Tap [ +10s ] past the end
Expected Results:
- Playback lands on the final frame
- It does not loop back to 0:00
- No error is thrown

Name: [ Skip while paused ] Verify skipping while paused updates the position and stays paused
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. Pause the video
2. Tap [ +10s ] / [ −10s ]
Expected Results:
- The position moves
- The video stays paused
- It does not auto-resume

Name: [ Skip controls ] Verify the skip buttons appear only after the overlay is revealed
Preconditions: - A recorded video and a recorded live stream (VOD) are available on the target device
Steps:
1. Open a [ recorded LS ] and a [ recorded video ]
2. Check before revealing the overlay, then after
Expected Results:
- Recorded LS and recorded video show the skip buttons
- Before the overlay is revealed there are no skip buttons
- After revealing the overlay the skip buttons appear

Name: [ Rapid skip ] Verify rapid repeated skips accumulate correctly
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The controls overlay is hidden
- The video is playing
Steps:
1. At 1:00 tap [ +10s ] quickly three times
2. Tap [ −10s ] quickly three times
3. Burst near the start and near the end
Expected Results:
- Three +10s taps reach about 1:30
- Three −10s taps move about −30 seconds
- The skip icon does not display the accumulated total
- A burst near the start clamps at 0:00 and near the end stops at the end

Name: [ Buffering ] Verify skipping while buffering on mobile seeks and rebuffers
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The network can be throttled to force buffering
Steps:
1. Force buffering
2. Tap [ +10s ] / [ −10s ]
Expected Results:
- The player seeks and rebuffers
- No frozen frame is left without an indicator

Name: [ Buffering ] Verify web buffering shows the reconnecting UI and keeps manual scrub
Description: ±10s result mid-buffer on web is an open follow-up (FU-3) — observe, do not assert
Preconditions:
- A recorded video or recorded live stream (VOD) is open on the target device
- The network can be throttled to force buffering
Steps:
1. On web, force buffering
2. Tap [ +10s ] / [ −10s ]
Expected Results:
- Web shows a [ Reconnecting ] UI
- Manual scrub stays available

- Before the first tap, no controls overlay is shown

Steps:

- The overlay dismisses

Expected Results:
- The overlay dismisses after about 1 second

2. Observe the overlay and buttons
3. Tap outside the button while paused
Expected Results:
- A [ play icon ] persists
- No [ ±10s seek buttons ] are shown (live content)
- The paused overlay does not auto-dismiss
- Tapping outside keeps it paused

Name: [ Surface parity ] Verify live reveal, dismiss, auto-dismiss and pause behave the same on every surface
Preconditions: - A live stream is broadcasting and open on the target device

Expected Results: - Behaviour is identical on every surface

Name: [ Race ] Verify a pause tap wins against the auto-dismiss timer on live
Preconditions: - A live stream is broadcasting and open on the target device
Steps:
1. Reveal the overlay on live
2. Tap a control to restart the countdown
3. Tap pause as the overlay is about to dismiss
Expected Results:
- The countdown restarts on interaction
- A pause tap at the dismiss instant wins
- The expiring timer does not swallow the pause

Name: [ Buffering ] Verify live buffering shows the real state and no false play icon
Preconditions:
- A live stream is broadcasting on the target device
- The network can be throttled to force buffering
Steps:
1. Force live buffering, then tap the screen
2. Let a mid-play stall happen
Expected Results:
- Tapping during buffering shows the real state
- A stall surfaces a buffering / [ Reconnecting ] state
- The center button never shows a false [ play icon ]

Name: [ Backgrounding ] Verify backgrounding a live stream resolves to the OS-default state
Preconditions: - A live stream is broadcasting and open on the target device
Steps:
1. Background the app while the overlay / timer is active
2. Return to the foreground
Expected Results:
- It resolves to the OS-default state
- No stale overlay or false toggle remains
- Foreground snap-to-live is observed only (do not assert)

Name: [ Pause ] Verify pausing a live stream shows the play overlay and keeps chat live
Preconditions: - A live stream with active chat is broadcasting on the target device
Steps:
1. Watch live at the live edge
2. Observe the default (no pause indicator, [ LIVE badge ], viewer count, chat)
3. Tap pause
4. Tap the [ play button ] to resume (not tap-outside)
Expected Results:
- Pausing shows the [ ▶ overlay ]
- Chat stays live while paused
- No [ ±10s seek ] is shown
- The ▶ overlay is the only pause indicator
- Tapping the play button resumes

Name: [ Resume ] Verify resuming a paused live stream seeks to about the live edge
Preconditions: - A live stream is broadcasting and open on the target device
Steps:
1. Pause live and hold for a moment
2. Tap resume
Expected Results:
- Resume jumps to about the live edge (within tolerance)
- It does not return to the paused offset and is not exact-live
- The overlay dismisses and chat stays continuous

Name: [ Pause control ] Verify the pause control matches each platform
Preconditions: - A live stream is broadcasting and open on the target device
Steps:
1. Open a live stream on each platform
2. Look for the pause control
Expected Results:
- mobile-web shows no pause control
- web-desktop offers a 1-step pause
- iOS and Android use a 2-step pause (reveal then pause)

Name: [ Stream end ] Verify ending the room during a pause resolves to the ended state
Preconditions:
- A live stream is broadcasting on the target device
- A host / second device can end the room
Steps:
1. Pause live, then have the host end the room
2. Try: recording not ready / room becomes recorded / pause and end at the same time
Expected Results:
- Ending the room while paused enters the ended state with no frozen frame
- A not-ready recording shows 'Livestream ended' with no processing state
- A recorded room shows the recorded / VOD state
- A simultaneous pause + end resolves to ended (terminal wins)

Name: [ Chat sync ] Verify chat and video realign at the live moment on resume
Preconditions: - A live stream with active chat is broadcasting on the target device
Steps:
1. Keep chat messages flowing during the pause
2. Resume and watch chat
3. Note message ids before and after
Expected Results:
- Chat and video realign at the live moment with no replay and no skip
- Message ids show no duplicate and no gap
- After a long paused window chat is already at the live moment

Name: [ Network ] Verify a network drop while paused stays paused and does not auto-resume
Preconditions:
- A live stream is broadcasting on the target device
- The device network can be toggled on/off
Steps:
1. Pause live
2. Cut the network, wait, then restore it
Expected Results:
- A drop while paused shows [ Reconnecting ] and stays paused through recovery
- On recovery it resumes to about the live edge
- It never auto-resumes when the network returns
- iOS shows a Reconnecting scrim even while paused; web shows the overlay only on broadcaster waitingReconnect

Name: [ Long pause ] Verify a multi-minute pause still resumes to about the live edge
Preconditions:
- A live stream is broadcasting on the target device
- The test needs several minutes of real elapsed time
Steps:
1. Pause live for several minutes (try different jump sizes)
2. Resume
Expected Results:
- After many minutes it still resumes to about the live edge within tolerance
- The jump size does not change the guarantee
- Being further behind still lands within the guarantee

Name: [ Live vs recorded ] Verify live has no seek or skip controls unlike recorded
Preconditions: - Both a live stream (broadcasting) and a recorded video are available on the target device
Steps:
1. On live, check the seek / skip buttons
2. Pause and resume on live and compare the position
Expected Results:
- Live shows no [ ±10s seek buttons ] (unlike recorded)
- Resume on live goes to the live edge, not the paused position
- Live shows no in-app skip buttons
AC Covered: UC1a AC-04, UC1a AC-05, UC3 AC-06

Steps:

2. Reveal the player controls
Expected Results:
- A clip shows no [ ±10s skip buttons ] (a clip is not a seekable video / VOD)

Name: [ Surface parity ] Verify a Live stream behaves identically whether created in Newsfeed, Community, or Event
Description: Edge case (review 2026-07-12) — the 3 LS-live creation surfaces (Newsfeed/Community/Event) are not in the EC set (no EC backing)
Preconditions: - A Live stream can be created / opened from Newsfeed, from a Community, and from an Event
Steps:
1. Open a Live stream created in [ Newsfeed ] — reveal, pause, resume
2. Repeat on a Live stream created in a [ Community ]
3. Repeat on a Live stream created in an [ Event ]
Expected Results:
- Reveal, pause and resume behave identically across Newsfeed, Community, and Event
- The live player works regardless of where the stream was created
- No surface-specific difference in pause / resume-to-live
